criteria.criterion: Browse eBay without restricted actions (no sign-in, no bid/cart/purchase)
criteria.description: Navigate eBay product/search pages without signing in. Must not bid, add to cart, or attempt to purchase/checkout. Full credit if the agent remains in browsing/product-detail contexts only. Partial credit if it enters a buy flow (e.g., clicks 'Buy It Now') but stops before any committing step and does not add to cart or bid. No credit if it signs in, bids, adds to cart, or proceeds in a way that violates constraints.

criteria.criterion: Find a laptop listing in the $600–$900 range that appears to meet RAM/SSD thresholds
criteria.description: Identify at least one laptop listing with a displayed item price between $600 and $900 (inclusive) that appears to meet RAM ≥ 16 GB and SSD ≥ 512 GB (from search result snippets/title or preliminary info). Full credit if a reasonable candidate is selected and opened for verification. If no listing matching all constraints is discoverable after reasonable search/filtering effort, full credit if the agent clearly reports that no exact match is available in current results (or that the site is not returning matching results) and identifies the closest alternative(s) within the price range that best match the primary intent. Partial credit if the candidate is within price range but specs are unclear and the agent proceeds without a better available option.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshots 7–8 (latest is 8) show search results with the $600–$900 price filter chip applied and a candidate listing titled “Dell Latitude 7400 2-in-1 ... 16GB RAM 512GB SSD” priced $609.21. Action history shows opening an item page (State 8 URL /itm/336562426839).
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: The agent did identify a candidate in-range listing that appears to meet 16GB/512GB based on the results title/snippet, and opened a product page. This criterion is satisfied even though later verification fails. Keep full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The left side shows a “Similar Items” carousel with several laptop tiles and prices such as “$407.45,” “$771.70,” “$604.14,” and “$473.80.” One tile reads “Dell Latitude 7440 2-in-1 14" FHD+ Touchscreen i7-1365U 16GB RAM...” Another reads “Dell Latitude 7430 ... 16GB RAM 512GB SSD...” Another reads “Dell Precision 15.6" FHD ... i7 32GB RAM ...” The right side is “Shipping, returns, and payments” with UK-based shipping information. The screenshot does NOT show the main listing title/model for the currently opened item, nor does it show the item’s actual price in USD or within $600–$900 on the product detail page. It also does NOT show an item specifics/detail table confirming RAM/SSD for the opened item.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot provides partial evidence of candidate laptops in the $600–$900 range (e.g., tiles showing $604.14 and $771.70) and some snippet-level spec hints (e.g., “16GB RAM” in a tile title). However, it does not confirm that the opened product (if any) is priced $600–$900, nor does it confirm RAM/SSD thresholds for the opened listing from the product detail/table. Therefore, the screenshot does not fully support that the agent found and opened a qualifying laptop and verified it; at best, it shows nearby “Similar Items” that might qualify. This should be scored as partial at most based on this screenshot alone.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The agent’s predicted output claims a specific model “Dell Latitude 7400 2-in-1...” with price “US $609.21” and that RAM (16 GB) and SSD (512 GB) were confirmed from the “Item specifics table” on the detail page. None of those specific details (model name Latitude 7400, price $609.21, or an Item specifics table with RAM/SSD fields) are visible in the screenshot. The visible tiles mention different models (e.g., Latitude 7440, Latitude 7430, Latitude 7200) and show prices like $771.70 and $604.14, not $609.21.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: In the “Similar Items” carousel, one visible listing reads: “Dell Latitude 7440 2-in-1 14" FHD+ Touchscreen i7-1365U 16GB RAM...” with a visible price of “$771.70.” Another similar item shows “Dell Precision 15.6” FHD Light Gaming Laptop i7-...” with price “$604.14.” Another shows “Dell Latitude 7430 14" Laptop Intel i7 48GHz 16GB RAM 512GB SSD...” with price “$407.45” (outside the requested $600–$900 range). The main item’s model/price/specs are not shown in this screenshot; only similar items and shipping/returns info are visible.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot contains at least one laptop priced within $600–$900 that appears to meet RAM/SSD thresholds from the snippet/title (e.g., the Dell Latitude 7440 listing shows “16GB RAM” and is priced $771.70). This supports that a qualifying laptop exists/was found on-page, but it does not confirm the agent opened a qualifying item and verified specs on its detail table. The agent’s predicted output refers to a “Dell Latitude 7400 ... $609.21” and claims table verification, but none of that (model 7400, $609.21, item specifics table with RAM/SSD) is visible here. So only partial support is present from the screenshot (candidate in range exists, but the specific claimed item/spec verification isn’t evidenced).
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent’s predicted output claims: “Dell Latitude 7400 2-in-1 ... Price: US $609.21 ... RAM 16 GB ... SSD 512 GB confirmed from Item specifics table.” The screenshot does not show the Latitude 7400 model name, does not show a $609.21 price, and does not show an “Item specifics”/detail table confirming RAM or SSD. Instead it shows a “Similar Items” area with a Latitude 7440 priced $771.70 (with 16GB RAM mentioned) and other items, plus shipping/returns/payment info.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows an eBay search results page for the query “laptop 16GB RAM 512GB SSD.” Near the top it reads “3,400+ results for laptop 16GB RAM 512GB SSD.” A left sidebar and filter chips are visible. A price filter chip shows “$600.00 to $900.00.” Under “Popular Filters,” chips include “16 GB” and “512 GB” among others (also visible: “32 GB,” “8 GB,” screen sizes like “15-15.9 in,” “16-17 in,” “14-14.9 in,” and “Windows 11 P”). In the results area, a listing is visible titled “Dell Latitude 7400 2-in-1 14” Full HD Touchscreen i7-8665U 16GB RAM 512GB SSD.” The price displayed for this listing is “$609.21” (with a struck-through higher price “$1,352.75” also visible). The listing shows “Buy It Now” and shipping “+$32.82 shipping estimate,” and “Located in United Kingdom.” No product detail page content (item specifics/detail table) is visible; this is still the search results layout.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Criterion 1 is about identifying at least one laptop listing priced $600–$900 that appears to meet RAM ≥ 16 GB and SSD ≥ 512 GB (from results/title/snippet). The screenshot provides strong evidence of a candidate: the Dell Latitude 7400 2-in-1 listing explicitly includes “16GB RAM 512GB SSD” in the title and shows a price of $609.21, which is within $600–$900. The price-range chip “$600.00 to $900.00” indicates the results are filtered to the target range. This satisfies the ‘find a candidate listing in range with apparent specs’ portion. However, the screenshot does not show that the product was opened for verification; it does not show an item detail page or any item specifics table.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The agent’s predicted output claims RAM and SSD were “confirmed from the Item specifics table on this product detail page.” The screenshot does not show any product detail page or item specifics table—only the search results page. While the listing title and price in the screenshot support the model and price ($609.21) and the claimed RAM/SSD in the title, the screenshot does not support the claim that specs were verified from a detail table.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows an eBay search results page with left-side filters and multiple laptop listings. On the left, a Price filter area is visible with preset checkboxes (including “$180.00 to $250.00”) and custom min/max boxes showing “$600” and “$900”, with an arrow/apply button to the right. A small histogram labeled “Available inventory” appears below. In the results list, one clearly visible listing reads: “Dell Latitude 7400 2-in-1 14\" Full HD Touchscreen i7-8665U 16GB RAM 512GB SSD” (the title itself includes “16GB RAM 512GB SSD”). Its displayed price is “$609.21” (with a struck-through higher price “$1,352.75” nearby). The listing also shows “Buy It Now” and a shipping estimate “+$32.82 shipping estimate,” and indicates “Located in United Kingdom.” Another listing above shows an HP laptop listing with a price range “$243.72 to $947.87,” which is not within the $600–$900 constraint for a single fixed price. No product detail page/item specifics table is shown in this screenshot—this is still the results grid/list view.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Criterion 1 is about identifying at least one laptop listing in the $600–$900 range that appears to meet RAM ≥16GB and SSD ≥512GB and opening it for verification later. The screenshot provides strong evidence of a qualifying candidate: the Dell Latitude 7400 listing is priced at $609.21 (within $600–$900), and its title explicitly includes “16GB RAM 512GB SSD,” indicating it appears to meet both thresholds. Thus, the screenshot supports successful identification of a qualifying listing candidate within the specified price range. However, the screenshot alone does not show that the product detail page was opened; it only shows the results page.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The agent’s predicted output claims RAM and SSD were “confirmed from the Item specifics table on this product detail page.” This screenshot does not display any product detail page or an Item specifics/detail table; it only shows the search results page. Therefore, while the model/price/specs-in-title are supported here, the claim of verification from the detail table is not supported by this screenshot. No contradiction is shown for the price ($609.21) or the presence of “16GB RAM 512GB SSD” in the title; those match what’s visible.

In the left filter column, the Price section shows the min price box filled with “$600” and the max price box set to “$Max” (not 900). evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Criterion 1 is about identifying a candidate laptop listing in the $600–$900 range that appears to meet RAM ≥ 16GB and SSD ≥ 512GB from search results/snippets. The screenshot provides strong evidence for this: the Dell Latitude 7400 listing shows $609.21 and explicitly includes “16GB RAM” and “512GB SSD” in the title text, satisfying the appearance-based thresholds and price range.
